newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 10.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 10. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto agreed that terrorism must be opposed.

Indonesia mining analysts said the government should quickly solve the conflict between Canada's Bre-X Minerals and Barrick Gold Corp over the potentially huge Busang gold mine in East Kalimantan to maintain foreign investor confidence.
Bank Indonesia said depositors would only be paid after preferred creditors whenever a bank is liquidated. Preferred creditors are those who hold liens on a bank's fixed assets.
Transmigration Minister Siswono Yudohusodo said the recent riots in the multi-ethnic nation were symptoms of a sick society.
Some 963 Indonesian workers deported by the Malaysian government arrived in Tanjung Perak harbour on Thursday. Most of the people live in East Java and illegally entered Malaysia.
